# Menu

> A button that opens a list of actions. It's the APG's menu button, keyboard and all.

`<slab-menu>` · Navigation · built on `[role=menu] + [popover]`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/menu/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/menu.js';
import 'slab-elements/menu.item.js';
import 'slab-elements/menu.group.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-menu label="File">
  <button slot="anchor">File</button>

  <slab-menu-item>New</slab-menu-item>
  <slab-menu-item>Open…</slab-menu-item>
  <slab-menu-item disabled>Save</slab-menu-item>
</slab-menu>
```

To do something when a Menu Item is chosen, listen for its "click".

A Menu Item with `type="checkbox"` or `type="radio"` is a `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, and a click checks it before your "click" listener hears it. Put each set of radios in a `slab-menu-group` with a `label`, so they're named together and a click unchecks only the radios in that group.

```html
<slab-menu label="View">
  <button slot="anchor">View</button>

  <slab-menu-item type="checkbox" checked>Show grid</slab-menu-item>

  <slab-menu-group label="Units">
    <slab-menu-item type="radio" checked>Metric</slab-menu-item>
    <slab-menu-item type="radio">Imperial</slab-menu-item>
  </slab-menu-group>
</slab-menu>
```

## Submenus

Put a `slab-menu` inside another, with a `slab-menu-item` in its `anchor` slot, to make a submenu. Its Menu Item is one of its parent's, and opens it beside the parent. Give the submenu a `label`, usually the same as its Menu Item's.

```html
<slab-menu label="File">
  <button slot="anchor">File</button>

  <slab-menu-item>New</slab-menu-item>

  <slab-menu label="Share">
    <slab-menu-item slot="anchor">Share</slab-menu-item>

    <slab-menu-item>Email</slab-menu-item>
    <slab-menu-item>Message</slab-menu-item>
  </slab-menu>
</slab-menu>
```

Resting the pointer on a submenu's Menu Item for a moment opens it, and moving on to another of its parent's Menu Items closes it after the same moment, so the pointer can cut across on its way in. A click on a Menu Item in a submenu closes every Menu it's in.

## Keyboard

| Key                | What it does                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space, Down | On the anchor, opens the menu at the first Menu Item.                         |
| Up                 | On the anchor, opens the menu at the last Menu Item.                          |
| Up, Down           | Moves to the previous or next Menu Item, wrapping and skipping disabled ones. |
| Home, End          | Moves to the first or last Menu Item.                                         |
| A character        | Moves to the next Menu Item whose label starts with what's typed.             |
| Enter, Space       | Clicks the active Menu Item and closes the menu, or opens its submenu.        |
| Escape             | Closes the menu and returns focus to the anchor.                              |
| Tab                | Closes the menu and moves focus on.                                           |
| Right              | On a Menu Item with a submenu, opens it at its first Menu Item.               |
| Left               | In a submenu, closes it and returns focus to its Menu Item.                   |
| Escape             | In a submenu, closes only the submenu and returns focus to its Menu Item.     |

## Elements

### `<slab-menu>`

Import `slab-elements/menu.js` to register it.

A menu with no visual styles: a button that opens a list of Menu Items, to act on one.

It's the APG's menu button. There's no native menu, so the Menu Items are in a `[role=menu]` element in a native `[popover="auto"]`, opened from whatever is slotted into `anchor`. A click on the anchor, or Enter or Space, opens it at the first Menu Item, and the Up arrow opens it at the last. The anchor gets `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, which a Slab anchor, such as a Copy Button, passes on to its own button.

Focus moves to the menu while it's open, and its `aria-activedescendant` points at the active Menu Item. The Up and Down arrows move through the Menu Items, wrapping and skipping disabled ones, Home and End go to the first and last, and typing moves to the next one whose label starts with what was typed. Hovering a Menu Item makes it the active one, as in the APG's examples. Enter, Space and a click click the Menu Item and close the menu. Escape and Tab close it, Escape returning focus to the anchor.

A Menu inside a Menu, with a Menu Item as its anchor, is a submenu. It's one of its parent's Menu Items, so the arrow keys and typeahead land on it, and it opens beside it rather than below. Enter, Space, a click and the Right arrow open it at its first Menu Item, and so does resting the pointer on its Menu Item for a moment. Left and Escape close it and return focus to its parent, and the pointer moving off to another of its parent's Menu Items closes it after the same moment. Clicking a Menu Item in a submenu closes every Menu it's in, as does Tab. In a right-to-left page, Left and Right swap.

The popover is placed beside the anchor with CSS anchor positioning, the way Popover's is. `placement` picks the side and nothing else.

Style it through its parts and `:state(open)`, and each Menu Item through the states Menu Item sets.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type                                     | Default    | Description                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`                                 |            | Names the menu.                                                                                                                        |
| `open`             | `boolean`                                | `false`    | Whether it's open. Set it to open or close it.                                                                                         |
| `placement`        | `'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'top'` | `'bottom'` | The side of its anchor it opens on, when there's room. It flips when there isn't. A submenu ignores it and opens beside its Menu Item. |

#### Properties

| Name                | Type         | Description               |
| ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `items` (read-only) | `MenuItem[]` | Its Menu Items, in order. |

#### Methods

| Signature                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hide(): void`                     | Closes it.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `show(): void`                     | Opens it.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `toggle(force?: boolean): boolean` | Opens it when it's closed, and closes it when it's open, as a native popover's `togglePopover()` does. `true` only opens it and `false` only closes it. Returns whether it's open. |

#### Events

| Name           | Type          | Description                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toggle`       | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does. |
| `beforetoggle` | `ToggleEvent` | Before it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` that doesn't bubble. Cancel it while it's opening to keep it closed.   |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                            | Description                                                               |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `anchor`  | `Element`                       | What opens the menu, usually a \`<button>\`, or a Menu Item for a submenu |
| (default) | `MenuItem \| MenuGroup \| Menu` |                                                                           |

#### CSS parts

| Name      | Description            |
| --------- | ---------------------- |
| `menu`    | The Menu Items         |
| `popover` | What the menu opens in |

#### CSS states

| Name              | Description                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(open)`    | While it's open.                                           |
| `:state(submenu)` | While it's a submenu, opened from an item of another Menu. |

### `<slab-menu-item>`

Import `slab-elements/menu.item.js` to register it.

A Menu Item with no visual styles. The host is the menu item, so style it directly.

Listen for "click" on it to act on it. Its Menu clicks it for Enter and Space, the way a button is clicked from the keyboard, and closes once it has. A disabled Menu Item isn't clicked, again like a button.

`type="checkbox"` makes it a `menuitemcheckbox`, which a click checks or unchecks. `type="radio"` makes it a `menuitemradio`, which a click checks, unchecking the other radio Menu Items beside it. Put each set of radios in a Menu Group, so they're named together and kept apart from the rest. Either way, it's checked or unchecked before any "click" listener hears the click, as a native checkbox is, so a listener reads the new `checked`.

It's never focused. Focus stays on its Menu, which points at the active Menu Item with `aria-activedescendant`.

Its Menu sets `:state(active)`. It sets `:state(checked)` and `:state(disabled)` itself. Nothing is drawn for a check: that's a mark a design makes.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type                              | Default  | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`    | `string`                          |          | Names the Menu Item in place of its text, and is what typeahead matches against.                                              |
| `checked`  | `boolean`                         | `false`  | Whether a checkbox or radio Menu Item is checked. Ignored for any other.                                                      |
| `disabled` | `boolean`                         | `false`  | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted. |
| `type`     | `'checkbox' \| 'item' \| 'radio'` | `'item'` | "checkbox" for an item that's checked and unchecked, "radio" for one that's checked within its Menu Group, or "item".         |

#### Properties

| Name               | Type     | Description                                                                               |
| ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text` (read-only) | `string` | What the user reads as the Menu Item's name: its label, or its text when it has no label. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                                                |
| --------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | The label, plus anything else a design puts in a Menu Item |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(active)`   | While it's the active one, which the keyboard moves through while focus stays on its container. |
| `:state(checked)`  | While it's checked.                                                                             |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                            |

### `<slab-menu-group>`

Import `slab-elements/menu.group.js` to register it.

A Menu Group with no visual styles: a named `[role=group]` of Menu Items, such as a set of radio Menu Items, inside a Menu or a Context Menu.

The host is the group, so style it directly. Its Menu Items are still its Menu's, so the arrow keys and typeahead move through them as through the rest, and a radio Menu Item unchecks only the other radios in its group.

Its label is rendered, for sighted users, and hidden from screenreaders, which hear it as the group's name from `aria-label` instead. `hide-label` hides it visually too.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                    |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type       | Description |
| --------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| (default) | `MenuItem` |             |

#### CSS parts

| Name    | Description |
| ------- | ----------- |
| `label` | The label   |
